title: Body systems: the dispatch challenge
subtitle: Two systems, different jobs, one working body
objective: Describe digestion and circulation, then explain how they work together.

sow.exactOutcome: Describe the main human body systems (circulation, digestion).
sow.alignment: Directly develops this stated outcome with secondary-age tasks at an upper-KS2 conceptual level. Support and stretch are flexible; this exemplar is not a claim of qualification approval.

priorLearning: Know that food contains substances the body uses.
success: Match organs to the digestive or circulatory system.
Explain that digestion breaks food down and circulation transports substances.
Repair a model that sends whole food into blood vessels.

vocabulary.meaning: A body part made of tissues that carries out particular jobs.
Organs working together to carry out major jobs.
Breaking food into smaller substances that can be absorbed.
The movement of blood through the heart and blood vessels.
A substance the body needs for energy, growth or other functions.

equipment: Shared evidence sheet and selected route; pencils; optional reusable organ/job cards.
preparation: Print one shared evidence sheet per pupil; cut cards only if useful.
Preview the two-system model. It is a job map, not an anatomical picture.
safety: No food, bodily samples, exercise or personal health measurements are needed.
Allow pupils to use labels rather than draw an outline of their own body.
practicalAlternative: All work is a paper or screen model using supplied organ/job cards.

misconceptions.correction: The digestive system breaks food down; the heart pumps blood.
misconceptions.check: Ask which organ squeezes to pump blood.

misconceptions.claim: Pieces of sandwich travel around blood vessels.
misconceptions.correction: Small absorbed nutrients travel in blood; recognisable food pieces stay in the digestive tract.
misconceptions.check: Ask whether a blood vessel contains a whole bread crumb.

misconceptions.claim: One organ does every job in a system.
misconceptions.correction: Several organs contribute different jobs to the same system.
misconceptions.check: Ask why mouth and small intestine are both needed.

access.supported: Match organ and job cards; use two sentence frames.
access.standard: Build and explain a two-system job map.
access.stretch: Repair a misleading museum display and explain the model boundary.
access.regulation: Offer quiet pointing, private writing, drawing or adult scribing. Pass-and-return for public questions. Use fictional cases; no personal medical disclosure or comparison of bodies. Assign response routes from current evidence, not fixed pupil labels.

sources.title: NIDDK: Your digestive system and how it works
sources.note: Checked September 2026. Digestion, absorption, transport and water absorption. Paraphrased factual reference; diagrams and activities are original.

sources.title: NHLBI: How blood flows through the heart
sources.note: Checked September 2026. Right-heart/lung/left-heart/body sequence and oxygenation. No adult pulse thresholds are used for pupils.

slides.title: A delivery puzzle
body: How does something from lunch reach a muscle?
Today: identify the two systems doing different jobs.
slides.notes: Give 20 seconds to think, draw or point. Do not require personal food talk. Say: We are tracing a fictional lunch, not judging anyone’s choices.

slides.title: Name it, then say its job
body: R1. Name an organ in the chest.
R2. Name an organ that handles food.
R3. Does naming an organ explain its job?
slides.notes: R1 heart or lungs; R2 mouth, stomach or intestine. R3 no; a job statement is also needed. Accept familiar language and supply scientific labels.

slides.title: I follow the food route
body: I find the organ. I read its job.
Chewing is one part of digestion.
The stomach does not finish every task.
slides.notes: Think aloud: I place mouth before stomach because food enters at the mouth. I add the small intestine because digestion continues and most nutrients are absorbed there. This is a selected job map; it does not show every organ or their shapes.

visual.title: Digestive system: a processing route
visual.description:
A simplified scientific sequence: Mouth
chews food; Stomach
mixes food; Small intestine
digests; absorbs. Also included: oesophagus, large intestine,
rectum and anus. This map shows selected jobs.

elements.text:
Also included: oesophagus, large intestine,
rectum and anus. This map shows selected jobs.

slides.title: I follow the transport route
body: The heart pumps blood.
Blood vessels form routes around the body.
Blood carries useful substances and some wastes.
slides.notes: Shared I do time. Trace clockwise. Think aloud: The system keeps blood moving; it does not chew or digest food. This simplified loop leaves out the lung route, which we investigate next lesson. It is not a complete circulatory route.

visual.title: Circulation: transport around a network
visual.description:
Clockwise sequence: Heart
pumps blood; Blood vessels
carry blood; Body tissues
receive substances; Blood vessels
return blood. Simplified job map: the lung route is omitted here.

elements.text: Simplified job map: the lung route is omitted here.

slides.title: I connect the two systems
body: Digestion supplies small absorbable substances.
Circulation transports absorbed nutrients.
I must change “food” to “small nutrients”.
slides.notes: Shared I do time. Model correction: “The heart sends sandwiches to muscles” becomes “Small absorbed nutrients are carried in blood to tissues.” Digestion and circulation are distinct but linked. Teacher nuance: most dietary fat first enters lymph; this core model follows a soluble nutrient such as glucose.

visual.title: Where the systems connect
visual.description:
A simplified scientific sequence: Food in
small intestine; Small absorbed
nutrients; Blood carries
to body tissues. The gut wall is crossed by small substances.
A whole sandwich does not enter a blood vessel.

elements.text:
The gut wall is crossed by small substances.
A whole sandwich does not enter a blood vessel.

slides.title: Organ-and-job dispatch
body: Use evidence cards A–F.
Sort A–E into digestive or circulatory.
W1. Explain one placement using the job.
slides.notes: Work in pairs or independently with pointing. Read each card once. Mouth, stomach, small intestine digestive; heart and blood vessels circulatory. Ask pupils to justify a disputed placement. Cards are on pupil page 1.

slides.title: The mixed-up display
body: Display: “Stomach pumps blood. Heart breaks food down.”
W2. Replace both job labels.
Use a card as your reason.
slides.notes: Shared We do time. Invite pupils to move labels or read a repaired statement. Answer: stomach mixes food with digestive juices; heart pumps blood. A vague “stomach eats” needs refining.

slides.title: Check the delivery claim
body: Display: “Bread crumbs travel inside blood vessels.”
W3. Keep, reject or repair this claim.
Show the link between two systems.
slides.notes: Shared We do time. Reject as written; digested small nutrients, for example glucose, can be absorbed and transported by blood. Praise correct links, not speed.
slides.reveal: Small absorbed nutrients travel in blood; whole food pieces do not.

slides.title: Which explanation links the systems?
body: Choose, then explain one word.
slides.notes: A: confuses jobs. B correct and connects both. C: organs do not work alone. Re-teach with two cards, one for processing and one for transporting.

options.feedback: The heart pumps blood; digestive organs digest food.

options.text: Digestion produces small nutrients; blood transports them.
options.feedback: This gives the two different, connected jobs.

options.text: The stomach works without any other body system.
options.feedback: Systems work together; tissues also need a blood supply.

slides.title: Build the museum panel
body: Choose supported, standard or stretch.
Use page 1 as your evidence.
Your panel must explain both systems.
slides.notes: 10 minutes across three slides. All routes assess organ jobs and the connection. A drawing with dictated labels is valid independent evidence.

slides.title: A useful sentence frame
body: “The ____ belongs to the ____ system.”
“Its job is ____.”
“The two systems connect because ____.”
slides.notes: Shared You do time. Prompt by asking what happens to food and what moves blood. Do not fill the gaps for pupils.

slides.title: Proofread for science
body: Have I mixed up digestion and pumping?
Have I explained the link?
Does my arrow carry a small substance?
slides.notes: Shared You do time. Check pupils do not label whole-food arrows into blood. Stretch should name a limitation: omitted organs, approximate positions or omitted lymph route.

slides.title: Museum quality check
body: Read or show one repaired statement.
Does it name a job and a system?
Improve one label after feedback.
slides.notes: 4 minutes across Review. Offer private teacher sharing. Model feedback: Your heart label is right; now explain what carries nutrients away.

slides.title: Choose the next question
body: Which organ would help explain transport next?
Suggest one question about its job.
slides.notes: Lundy: collect a pointed, spoken or written question. Teacher chooses one question about the heart’s route for next lesson and tells pupils how their suggestion shaped the starter.

slides.title: Leave a clear explanation
body: E1. Give the heart’s job.
E2. Give one digestive organ and its job.
E3. Explain how the two systems connect.
slides.notes: Heart pumps blood. Digestive organ with appropriate job. Digestion provides small absorbable nutrients that blood carries to tissues. Collect before public answers.

pupilPages.title: 1 • Shared evidence: body dispatch
pupilPages.intro: These are scientific job cards for a simplified model, not personal medical records.

cards.title: A • Mouth
cards.text: Chews food into smaller pieces; saliva begins digestion.

cards.title: C • Small intestine
cards.text: Continues digestion and absorbs most nutrients.

cards.title: E • Blood vessels
cards.text: Carry blood between the heart and body tissues.

cards.title: F • Delivery clue
cards.text: Absorbed small nutrients can enter blood and reach tissues. Food pieces do not enter blood vessels.

blocks.prompt: W1. Sort cards A–E into digestive or circulatory. Explain one placement.
W2. Repair: “Stomach pumps blood. Heart breaks food down.”
W3. Repair: “Bread crumbs travel inside blood vessels.”

pupilPages.title: 2 • Supported route: label the jobs
pupilPages.intro: Use page 1. Point, circle, draw or dictate.

blocks.prompt: S1. Which system includes the stomach?
S2. What does the heart do?
S3. Put A, B and C in food-route order. Name one job.
S4. Complete: Digestion makes some nutrients small enough to be ____ . Blood then ____ them to tissues. Word bank: transports / absorbed.
S5. Draw a two-system panel: one digestive organ, the heart and labelled job arrows.

pupilPages.title: 3 • Standard route: museum panel
pupilPages.intro: Use page 1. Make the body-system connection clear to a visitor.

blocks.prompt: N1. Complete the table. Use verbs that explain jobs.
N2. Describe a simplified food route through three organs.
N3. Explain how a nutrient can reach muscle tissue. Include digestion, absorption and blood.
N4. Repair the bread-crumb claim and explain why it was misleading.

pupilPages.title: 4 • Stretch route: repair the exhibit
pupilPages.intro: A visitor should leave with a useful model, not an incorrect shortcut.

blocks.prompt: T1. Write a 3-sentence panel linking digestion and circulation. Include named organs and the substance transported.
T2. A model has one box called “stomach” doing all digestion and pumping. Explain two changes it needs.
T3. Why is your panel still a simplified model? Name an omitted organ or process and explain the omission.
T4. Design one question to check whether a visitor understands the connection. Write your expected answer.

pupilPages.title: 5 • Exit and reflection
pupilPages.intro: Work independently; a labelled drawing or scribed explanation is welcome.

blocks.prompt: E1. What is the heart’s job?
E2. Name one digestive organ and explain its job.
E3. Explain how digestion and circulation work together.
E4. Suggest a question about the heart for the next lesson.
Reflection. Which misleading label did you improve?

answers.label: R1–R3
answers.answer: R1 heart or lungs. R2 stomach, mouth or an intestine. R3 no; a name identifies the part, whereas a job statement explains what it does.

answers.label: W1–W3
answers.answer: W1 A/B/C digestive; D/E circulatory, with job evidence. W2 stomach mixes food with digestive juices; heart pumps blood. W3 replace bread crumbs with small absorbed nutrients, for example glucose.

answers.label: Hinge A–C
answers.answer: A incorrect: heart pumps. B correct: different connected jobs. C incorrect: systems cooperate. Re-teach by tracing one food route and one blood route.

answers.label: S1–S5
answers.answer: S1 digestive. S2 pumps blood. S3 A→B→C; accept correct job. S4 absorbed; transports. S5 a named digestive organ with correct job, heart pumps blood and an arrow for small absorbed nutrients carried in blood; whole food into blood is incorrect.

answers.label: N1–N4
answers.answer: N1 mouth/digestive/chews; small intestine/digestive/digests and absorbs; heart/circulatory/pumps; vessels/circulatory/carry blood. N2 mouth→stomach→small intestine is an acceptable selected route; full route may include oesophagus. N3 small substances produced during digestion cross the gut wall and are carried in blood to muscle tissue. N4 food pieces remain in the gut; small absorbed nutrients travel in blood.

answers.label: T1–T4
answers.answer: T1 must distinguish digestion and circulation and explicitly connect absorption to transport. T2 add other digestive organs such as mouth and small intestine; replace pumping role with heart and vessels. T3 valid omissions include oesophagus, large intestine, lung route or detailed absorption. T4 an objective-aligned question such as “Does the heart digest food? Explain” with a correct expected response. Accept other accurate questions.

answers.label: E1–E4 / reflection
answers.answer: E1 pumps blood. E2 valid organ/job pair. E3 small absorbed nutrients from digestion are carried in blood to tissues. E4 testable or explanatory heart question, for example “Where does blood go after the heart?” Reflection has no prescribed preference.

answers.label: Assessment and re-teach
answers.answer: Secure: identifies at least one organ per system, gives correct jobs and explains the absorption–transport connection. If only organ names are secure, require one verb per organ. If whole-food transport persists, contrast food pieces with small dissolved nutrient particles.

teacherNotes: 40 minutes: opening 2; retrieval 3; I do 8; We do 8; hinge 3; You do 10; review 4; exit 2. Zero-minute slides share their stage time.
Supply shared page 1, one selected route page 2, 3 or 4, and page 5. Do not require all three routes. An independent spoken explanation can be recorded verbatim by an adult.
This lesson establishes system roles; the following heart lesson develops the double circulation, while the later transport lesson examines crossing the gut wall.

The job diagrams deliberately omit detailed anatomy and the complete circulatory route. Name that limitation. Do not teach that all dietary fats pass directly into blood: most enter the lymphatic system first.

Interactive We do uses predict, test and explain; paper cards W1–W3 provide the same decisions. A desk token can trace the model without an animated screen. Movement is optional and pupils control the pace.

interactive.title: Body dispatch: decide the next job
interactive.intro: Predict first, test the model, then explain using the evidence. Move at your own pace; paper W1–W3 tasks assess the same reasoning.
